page.text:
A group is *finite* when its underlying carrier set $X$ has finite
cardinality. The cardinality $|G| = |X|$ is called the *order* of the
group. The order of a finite group exerts immense control over its
internal substructure: by Lagrange's theorem and the Sylow theorems, the
arithmetic prime factorization of $|G|$ dictates the existence and sizes
of its subgroups.
